reading.title: What Makes a Strong Team?
reading.purpose: Learn how different strengths help a team finish a big job.
paras: A big job goes better with a strong team. Think about a class that plans a school garden, a crew that cleans a beach, or a band that puts on its first show. In each team, people bring different strengths.

Some people are ambitious. They set a high goal and keep everyone looking toward it. Others are industrious, which means they work hard and steadily, even when the job is dull. A dependable teammate does what was promised, so the team can count on every part being done.

Not every strength is about work. An outgoing teammate talks to new people and finds help, such as volunteers or free supplies. An adventurous teammate will try a new idea when the old way stops working. A sensible teammate asks, "Is this safe? Is it a good use of our time?"

Good teams also handle problems. A selfish teammate who takes all the best tools makes everyone angry. A sympathetic teammate notices when someone feels left out and says, "Come and help us." When people are cooperative, they share tools, share credit, and share the hard parts.
Remember that anyone can be capable of more than they expect. Ask what each person does best, give everyone a real job, and the team will often finish more than it planned.

qs.why: The sentence explains it: industrious people "work hard and steadily, even when the job is dull."

qs.q: Which sentence shows that a sympathetic teammate helps someone who feels left out?
choices: A sympathetic teammate notices when someone feels left out and says, "Come and help us."
An outgoing teammate talks to new people and finds help.
Ask what each person does best.
qs.why: This sentence names the feeling of being left out and shows the teammate inviting the person in.

ev.text: A sympathetic teammate notices when someone feels left out and says, "Come and help us."

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Only the most ambitious people can ever lead a team well.
Teams do best when people use different strengths and treat one another well.
A team should avoid trying a new idea when the old way fails.
Gardens, beaches, and bands are the only jobs a team can do.
qs.why: Every paragraph adds a strength or a way of treating teammates, and the last one says to give everyone a real job.

qs.q: A teammate keeps the best tools and will not share. Which word from the reading describes this person?
qs.why: The reading says a selfish teammate takes all the best tools, which makes everyone angry.
